back: A line whose points are all mapped onto themselves: none of them move.
Points move at right angles to the invariant line so that their distance from it is multiplied by the stretch factor $k$.

front: One-way stretch, factor $k$: image of $(x, y)$
notes: A stretch "parallel to the $x$-axis" has the $y$-axis invariant.

front: Two-way stretch with factors $a$ (parallel to the $x$-axis) and $b$ (parallel to the $y$-axis)
Effect of a one-way stretch with factor $k$ on area

back: Points move parallel to the invariant line, through a distance proportional to their distance from it.
notes: Points on opposite sides move in opposite directions.

back: $x$-axis invariant: $(x + ky, y)$. $y$-axis invariant: $(x, y + kx)$.

front: Effect of a shear on area
back: None: a shear keeps the same base and height, so the area is unchanged.
notes: A rectangle becomes a parallelogram of equal area.

front: How do you describe a stretch or a shear fully?
back: Name it, give the factor (stretch factor or shear factor) and the invariant line.
